title: How to Make Palak Kofta at Home: The Classic Shaam Savera Recipe Simplified
excerpt: Paneer-stuffed spinach dumplings in a smooth onion-tomato-cashew gravy — a show-stopping North Indian dish made without butter or cream.
body:
• Palak Kofta, also known as Shaam Savera, features paneer-stuffed spinach koftas in a cashew-enriched onion-tomato gravy — a North Indian classic popularized by chef Sanjeev Kapoor.
  • The dish gets its name from the contrast of dark spinach (shaam/evening) and white paneer (savera/dawn) visible when the koftas are sliced.
  • This simplified home version skips butter and cream, using cashews for richness and body in the gravy.
  • The koftas and gravy can be prepared a day ahead and assembled just before serving for easier weeknight or special-occasion cooking.

The Dish Behind the Name

Shaam Savera — evening and dawn — is one of Indian cuisine's most visually striking dishes. Created by celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor, it gets its poetic name from the dark green spinach exterior and pale paneer center of each kofta. Slice one open, and the contrast tells the story.

The dish combines elements of several North Indian favorites: the spinach-paneer pairing of palak paneer, the fried dumplings of malai kofta, and the smooth tomato-cashew gravy found in paneer butter masala. Yet it stands apart as a complete creation — earthy, mild, and richly textured without relying on heavy cream or butter.

Building the Koftas

The spinach covering starts with 200 grams of fresh spinach leaves, blended with one green chili, a teaspoon each of chopped garlic and ginger into a smooth puree. No water — excess moisture makes the mixture too loose to shape.

"Yet it stands apart as a complete creation — earthy, mild, and richly textured without relying on heavy cream or butter."

Half a cup of besan (gram flour) is dry-roasted over low heat for three to four minutes until aromatic, then mixed with the spinach puree. A quarter teaspoon of garam masala and salt go in, followed by 30 to 40 minutes of refrigeration to firm the mixture.

The paneer filling is 100 grams of grated paneer mixed with one and a half tablespoons of rice flour, quarter teaspoon garam masala, a pinch of nutmeg, and seven to eight saffron strands. Roll into small balls and refrigerate.

Assembly is straightforward: flatten a spinach portion, place a paneer ball in the center, seal the edges, and roll smooth. Coat each kofta in rice flour and refrigerate again for 20 to 30 minutes before frying in moderately hot oil until crisp and golden — about four to five minutes per batch.

The Cashew-Tomato Gravy

The gravy builds on a base of whole spices — tej patta, cinnamon, green and black cardamom, cloves, and shahi jeera — fried until aromatic. Three-quarter cup of chopped onions are sautéed until translucent, followed by ginger, garlic, and one and a half cups of chopped tomatoes.

Twelve large cashews go in with quarter teaspoon turmeric and one teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder. Add a cup of water and simmer until the tomatoes are fully softened. Remove the tej patta, cool, and blend to a fine paste.

Return to the pan, adjust consistency with water, add half a teaspoon of sugar and salt to taste. A crushed half teaspoon of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) goes in at the end for depth.

Bringing It Together

Slice each fried kofta in half with a sharp knife. Pour hot gravy into a serving bowl and arrange the halved koftas with paneer centers facing up. The contrast of dark green and white against the orange gravy is the signature visual.

Garnish with ginger juliennes and thin strips of green chili. A drizzle of cream is optional for richness.

The koftas are substantial — one to two per person is usually enough, served alongside roti, naan, tandoori roti, jeera rice, or peas pulao. Add the koftas to the gravy only at serving time; submerging them earlier softens the crisp covering.

Make-Ahead Tips

This is not a quick recipe, but it divides well across two days. The gravy keeps overnight in the refrigerator. The spinach mixture, paneer balls, or fully shaped uncooked koftas can also be prepared a day ahead and refrigerated. Coat shaped koftas with fresh rice flour just before frying if the coating has absorbed moisture. Leftover fried koftas reheat well in an oven or air fryer.
